definition: a basic food that forms a large part of a population's regular diet
example: Rice remains the staple for more than half of the world's population.

definition: a style of cooking that is typical of a country or region
example: Thai cuisine combines sweet, sour, salty and spicy flavours in a single dish.

definition: a rare or expensive food that is considered especially pleasant to eat
example: Sea urchin is regarded as a delicacy in coastal regions of Japan.

definition: one of the foods that are combined to make a particular dish
example: Fresh ingredients are the secret of many successful neighbourhood restaurants.

definition: food that is grown or raised on a farm, especially fruit and vegetables
example: Supermarkets now import fresh produce from every continent all year round.

definition: the gathering of crops, or the amount of crops gathered
example: A poor harvest following months of rain pushed up the price of wheat.

definition: the amount of a crop produced on a given area of land
example: New varieties of wheat have raised average yield per hectare by almost a third.

definition: farm animals such as cattle, sheep and pigs kept for food or work
example: Producing feed for livestock takes up a huge proportion of agricultural land.

definition: birds such as chickens and ducks kept for their meat or eggs
example: Demand for poultry has grown faster than demand for beef because it is cheaper.

definition: relating to milk and products made from it
example: Dairy farms in the region have struggled since milk prices fell.

definition: the small hard seeds of crops such as wheat, rice and maize
example: Global grain reserves fell sharply after two consecutive years of drought.

definition: a plant grown for its edible seeds, such as wheat, rice or oats
example: Cereal production must keep pace with a growing world population.

definition: describing land that is used or suitable for growing crops
example: Urban expansion is steadily reducing the amount of arable land near major cities.

definition: relating to farming and the cultivation of land
example: The country has shifted from an agrarian economy to one dominated by services.

definition: a farmer who works a very small piece of land
example: Smallholder farmers produce much of the food eaten in developing countries.

definition: large commercial companies involved in farming and food production
example: Powerful agribusiness corporations now control much of the global seed market.

definition: a level of production that provides just enough to live on
example: Millions of rural families depend on subsistence farming and have little left to sell.

definition: the growing of a single crop over a large area
example: Monoculture leaves a harvest dangerously exposed to a single disease.

definition: a chemical used to kill insects and other pests that damage crops
example: Heavy pesticide use can leave residues on fruit and vegetables.

definition: a substance added to soil to help crops grow better
example: Excess fertiliser washed from fields can pollute rivers and lakes.

definition: the artificial supply of water to land so that crops can grow
example: Efficient irrigation allows farmers to grow crops in regions with little rainfall.

definition: a long period with little or no rain, causing a shortage of water
example: A prolonged drought destroyed most of the maize crop last year.

definition: a severe shortage of food in a region, causing widespread hunger
example: War and poor governance can turn a poor harvest into a full-scale famine.

definition: suffering or death caused by a lack of food
example: Thousands of people faced starvation when supply routes were cut off.

definition: a condition caused by not eating enough of the right foods
example: Child malnutrition continues to stunt growth in the poorest regions of the world.

definition: not getting enough food or the right kind of food to stay healthy
example: Around eight hundred million people worldwide are still undernourished.

definition: the lack of reliable access to enough affordable and nutritious food
example: Food insecurity affects not only developing countries but also low-income families in rich nations.

definition: reliable access to enough affordable and nutritious food for all people
example: Climate change poses a growing threat to global food security.

definition: an amount that is more than is needed
example: Farmers in the region often sell their surplus at the weekly market.

definition: a situation in which something is not available in sufficient amounts
example: Scarcity of fresh water limits the amount of food some countries can grow.

definition: to build up a large supply of something for future use
example: Some governments stockpile grain to protect their citizens from sudden price rises.

definition: to prepare land and grow crops on it
example: Farmers in the highlands cultivate potatoes on steep terraced slopes.

definition: a system of agriculture that produces large amounts of food from a small area
example: Intensive farming can feed more people but often harms soil quality over time.

definition: a method of rearing animals indoors in large numbers to produce food cheaply
example: Critics of factory farming argue that crowded conditions cause animals needless suffering.

definition: describing animals that are allowed to move about freely outdoors
example: Free-range eggs usually cost more than those from caged hens.

definition: produced without artificial chemicals or fertilisers
example: Many shoppers will pay a premium for organic vegetables because they believe them to be safer.

definition: having had its genes changed artificially to give it useful qualities
example: Genetically modified crops can resist disease but remain controversial in many countries.

definition: the practice of growing different crops on the same land in a planned order
example: Crop rotation restores nutrients to the soil without the need for chemical fertilisers.

definition: a crop grown mainly to be sold rather than eaten by the farmer
example: Coffee is the principal cash crop for many smallholders in highland regions.

definition: an unusually large harvest
example: A bumper crop of apples caused prices to drop below the cost of production.

definition: describing farmland left unplanted for a time so that it can recover
example: Traditionally, farmers left a field fallow every third year to restore fertility.

definition: able to support healthy plant growth because the soil is rich
example: River floods deposit nutrients that keep the valley's soil fertile.

definition: too poor to support the growth of crops or plants
example: Overgrazing can turn productive pasture into barren ground within a few years.

definition: the feeding of animals on grass in open fields
example: Excessive grazing has stripped vegetation from large parts of the plateau.

definition: the farming of fish and other water creatures for food
example: Aquaculture now supplies about half of the fish eaten worldwide.

definition: catching so many fish that stocks cannot recover
example: Overfishing has pushed several species of tuna close to collapse.

definition: the use of machines to do work that was once done by hand
example: Mechanisation has dramatically cut the number of people needed to run a farm.

definition: having been changed by a series of industrial steps before being sold as food
example: Highly processed food is often cheaper than fresh alternatives but contains more salt and sugar.

definition: a substance added to food to stop it going bad
example: Some manufacturers have replaced artificial preservatives with natural alternatives such as vinegar.

definition: a substance added in small amounts to improve the taste, colour or life of food
example: Parents are increasingly wary of additives in snacks marketed to children.

definition: likely to go bad quickly if not kept cold or eaten soon
example: Perishable goods such as fish must be transported in refrigerated lorries.

definition: the length of time a product can be stored before it is no longer fit to sell or eat
example: Vacuum packaging extends the shelf life of meat by several days.

definition: the materials used to wrap and protect goods that are sold in shops
example: Excess packaging adds to household waste and is difficult to recycle.

definition: food that is thrown away instead of being eaten
example: Supermarkets are being urged to donate unsold products to cut down on food waste.

definition: the distance that food travels from where it is produced to where it is eaten
example: Buying from nearby farms helps reduce food miles and support the local economy.

definition: obtained from producers in the nearby area
example: The restaurant is proud that all of its vegetables are locally sourced.

definition: available or happening only at particular times of the year
example: Eating seasonal fruit is cheaper and generally tastes better than imported varieties.

definition: made in very large quantities by machines
example: Mass-produced bread lacks the character of loaves baked by a local baker.

definition: food that is prepared and served quickly in restaurants such as burger chains
example: The spread of fast food has changed eating habits in cities across the world.

definition: a prepared dish that only needs to be heated before eating
example: Busy commuters often rely on a ready meal rather than cooking from scratch.

definition: a meal bought at a restaurant to be eaten somewhere else
example: Ordering a takeaway has become a regular habit for many students.

definition: to eat a meal in a restaurant instead of at home
example: Families on tight budgets tend to dine out only on special occasions.

definition: prepared at home rather than bought ready-made or from a restaurant
example: A home-cooked meal is usually healthier and cheaper than a takeaway.

definition: a way of eating that includes the right amounts of all the necessary food types
example: A balanced diet should include plenty of vegetables, whole grains and lean protein.

definition: relating to the food that a person or group usually eats
example: Dietary habits in Asia have shifted towards more meat and dairy as incomes have risen.

definition: containing the substances needed for health and growth
example: School canteens are expected to provide nutritious meals at an affordable price.

definition: a substance that plants or animals need in order to live and grow
example: Overcooking vegetables can destroy many of the nutrients they contain.

definition: a unit of energy supplied by food
example: The typical adult needs roughly two thousand calories a day to maintain their weight.

definition: the amount of food served to one person at a meal
example: Restaurant portions in some countries are nearly twice the size of those served decades ago.

definition: the desire to eat food, or a strong wish for something
example: A short walk before dinner can stimulate the appetite.

definition: a person's ability to judge and enjoy the taste of food and drink
example: The dish was adapted to suit the palate of foreign tourists.

definition: tasting of salt or spices rather than being sweet
example: Some people prefer a savoury breakfast to the sweet cereals served in most households.

definition: having little or no taste or flavour
example: Hospital meals are often criticised for being bland and unappetising.

definition: the particular taste of a food or drink
example: Roasting the vegetables brings out a deeper flavour than boiling them.

definition: good for health and containing natural ingredients
example: The campaign encourages families to cook simple, wholesome meals together.

definition: safe and suitable to be eaten
example: Millions of tonnes of perfectly edible fruit are discarded because of minor blemishes.

definition: to have a strong desire for something, especially a particular food
example: Many people crave sugary snacks when they are tired or stressed.

definition: to allow oneself to enjoy something, especially food that is not healthy
example: Most nutritionists accept that it is fine to indulge occasionally.

definition: to undergo a chemical change in which sugars turn into alcohol or acid
example: Cabbage is left to ferment for several weeks to make kimchi.
